description:
1. Agent reads SKILL.md to discover the simple-anki-sync format, tag naming conventions, question templates, word limits, supplementary emoji guide, and the handle cross-reference system. 2. Agent reads bootcamp/week3/concurrency_brain_dump.txt and identifies the 6 major concept clusters (GIL, threading vs asyncio, concurrent.futures, asyncio internals, race condition vs deadlock, lock types). 3. Agent applies ATOMIZATION: splits compound concepts (e.g., GIL has 4 sub-facts) into separate cards, ensuring no card's English core answer exceeds 18 words (absolute limit) or ideally 9 words. 4. Agent uses STANDARDIZED QUESTION TEMPLATES: 'GIL definition' not 'What is the GIL?'; 'GIL CPU-bound behavior' not 'What happens with CPU-bound tasks under the GIL?'; 'threading vs asyncio pros/cons' etc. 5. Agent applies proper TAG FORMAT: #anki/programming/python_concurrency (English only, no Chinese). 6. Agent uses the simple-anki-sync TABLE FORMAT: two-row markdown table (question row + separator row + answer row) for every card. 7. Agent adds SUPPLEMENTARY INFO using

emoji content with correct emojis from the defined set (💡📝🔗⚡📊📅), keeping each supplementary block to 10-20 characters. 8. Agent uses the HANDLE SYSTEM (>) for at least one card that cross-references related concepts (e.g., a card about concurrent.futures referencing >ThreadPoolExecutor >ProcessPoolExecutor). 9. Agent ensures no card has more than 3 bullet points. 10. Output is saved as python_concurrency_cards.md in the workspace.
